One paragraph of the MDMA section still reads AI, the kidney one, and it is the card below. Every other paragraph of the section reads Human High by itself ([every check](https://github.com/u-dont-existDOTcom/joel-articles/blob/main/articles/bad-trips/humanize/h75-20261124/RESULTS.md)). After it the work goes down [the list of what is left](https://github.com/u-dont-existDOTcom/joel-articles/blob/main/articles/bad-trips/humanize/h75-20261124/LEFT.md).

suggestions.tested:
Five tries of mine by three methods, each keeping your five points in your order.

Tries 1 and 2 (turn 65), the warnings reworded: [Mixed](https://www.pangram.com/history/258a5b17-a2da-49d3-8da5-86655418be03), with your first two sentences Human Low and the rest AI, then [AI Generated](https://www.pangram.com/history/230891b4-4860-4f70-aa2b-f80f19baecb2) after one clause changed.

Try 3 (turn 66), from your text with the ways of your round-55 fixes: [AI Generated](https://www.pangram.com/history/e2566e53-84ec-45c7-880d-87b8cbdcecda).

Try 4 (this turn), a small fix for each of the four sentences two fresh readers agreed on: "... But they should be far more worried about the MDMA, since MDMA can cause acute kidney injury and rhabdomyolysis, on top of the overheating and dangerous electrolyte shifts. That makes kidney impairment a strong reason not to take MDMA, although once they've taken it, they still shouldn't sit there with worsening jaw tension. I just wouldn't tell somebody with serious kidney impairment to copy my one-gram-per-minute approach blindly, since that's a higher-risk situation where they should get help sooner." [AI Generated](https://www.pangram.com/history/7afc3e5b-d752-4d67-bf4c-41045d98fb45).

Try 5, another writer's rewrite from those readers' notes, in short plain statements: "... Kidney impairment is a strong reason to skip MDMA altogether. Once someone has taken it and their jaw tension is getting worse, the kidneys are no reason to sit there with it. Someone with serious kidney impairment should not copy my one-gram-per-minute approach blindly. Treat the situation as higher-risk and get help sooner." [AI Generated](https://www.pangram.com/history/f880b3a3-fb7c-4da4-828b-80b9f6bba5cf).
suggestions.sense: Two fresh readers ([their notes](https://github.com/u-dont-existDOTcom/joel-articles/blob/main/articles/bad-trips/humanize/h75-20261124/panel-b120/PANEL.md)) flagged four of its five sentences and said the same thing about the whole: a caution, a pivot, a list of risks, a contrast and a closing disclaimer, each given the same weight. Readers of the section also asked "get help sooner" than what, and one read "not a reason to sit there with worsening jaw tension" as "kidney problems are no reason to hold back magnesium", which your next sentence then takes back.
suggestions.why: Rewording each sentence didn't move the reading, so what reads AI is the order of the points and their even weight. Changing that means choosing which point leads, and saying what you'd have someone with bad kidneys do differently. I can't write that for you: it is a medical caution, and anything I added would be my advice under your name. How you'd say a caution also teaches me the guide's other cautions.
suggestions.advice_note: Edit it: what you'd tell someone with impaired kidneys whose jaw is tensing on MDMA, in your words and your order. If you can say what "get help sooner" means for them, or what you'd change about the one gram per minute, that answers both readers.
